body:
- **Jayaswal Neco**: textbook deleveraging (debt ₹3,845 cr to ₹1,496 cr), but **promoters have pledged 99.9%**. Disqualified.
- **KRBL**: debt down from 545 to 33 and OPM up to 19-21%, but there were governance concerns (a 2024 independent-director resignation and a promoter enforcement case). Market cap ₹9.6k cr is at the ceiling.
- **Manaksia Steels**: OPM step from 5% to 9-11% has no identified cause, and the board approved ₹800 cr of Haldia capex against a ₹760 cr market cap, so funding or dilution risk.
- **Emami Paper**: four-quarter OPM recovery (7% to 16%) at a 5.2x P/E, but debt of ₹933 cr is not falling and paper is cyclical.
- **Sportking India**: only two strong quarters (19-20% OPM), on a cotton-yarn spread. Cyclical.
- **Vardhman Special Steels**: five-quarter OPM step to 10-12%, but the promoter stake fell from 60% to 51% and equity capital rose from 82 to 97 (dilution). Watch.
- **Apcotex**: one 22% OPM quarter, then back to 12%. Lumpy.
- **Antelopus Selan**: strong E&P ramp-up, but reverse-merger dilution (equity 15 to 35) and FII exiting (3.9% to 0.45%).
- **Websol Energy**: margins falling (47% to 35%) on solar-cell oversupply. Opposite pattern.
- **Kernex Microsystems**: Kavach ramp-up, but CFO is negative, debtor days are 268, debt is rising and the promoter holds only 28.7%.
- **Welspun Enterprises**: one lumpy 37% OPM quarter and ₹2,100 cr debt.
- **Rashi Peripherals**: negative CFO and debt doubled.
- **EFC (I)**: equity diluted (10 to 30) and ₹1,386 cr debt.
- **Hariom Pipe, Lumax, Greenply, SSWL**: debt rising (and SSWL's P/E is about 30).
- **Chamanlal Setia**: single 21% OPM quarter on basmati. Watch only.
- **InfoBeans**: margins reverting to the FY22 level rather than a new step, and the promoter is trimming.
- **Madras Fertilizers**: PSU (85% government), 5% OPM.
- **Gokul Agro**: commodity trader at 3% OPM.
- **IMFA**: ferrochrome cyclical and FII holding falling.
- **Taal Tech**: debtor days up from 63 to 96.
- **Amrutanjan**: no growth and DII exiting (12.3% to 6.9%).
- **No inflection, or already well covered:** Fiem, Swaraj Engines, MPS, VRL Logistics, J Kumar, Vimta, Dynamic Cables, Bharat Seats, Pudumjee, Haldyn Glass, Jindal Drilling, R Systems (Blackstone overhang), TIIL (promoter at 74.7%).
- **Excluded as SME, micro-cap, holding company or finance company:** Kalind, Shera, APS, SJ Logistics, Resonance, Dynamic Services, Career Point Edu, SIL Investments, Kama Holdings, UY Fincorp, Unifinz, Nisus, Arman, Indus InvIT, Dolat Algotech.

body:
**Verified price block:** ₹487.75 close 19-Nov-2026 (screener chart).
- The screener series matches independent quotes exactly: ₹473.90 on 23-Oct (Kotak Neo ₹473.9), ₹507.90 on 27-Oct (Investing.com 507.90) and ₹526.55 on 5-Nov (Upstox ₹525.40 at 15:29 IST, an intraday snapshot).
- No independent quote dated 19-Nov was found, so the latest price is single-sourced but series-validated.
- Share count rose in July 2026: 92.23 lakh shares were issued preferentially at ₹470 to non-promoter institutions (Bandhan Small Cap, Emerge PO Trust, Cohesion MK). Q2 EPS 4.75 on PAT ₹58 cr implies about 12.2 cr shares.
- **Diluted mcap ≈ ₹5,955 cr. TTM P/E = 487.75 / 21.37 ≈ 22.8x on reported TTM EPS, or ≈ 24.2x on the post-issue share count.** I use 24x.

| ₹ cr | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 | TTM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 1,707 | 1,980 | 3,282 | 4,624 | 5,553 | 5,731 |
| OPM | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% |
| PAT | 25 | 36 | 82 | 149 | 213 | 246 |
| ROCE | 10% | 12% | 21% | 24% | 24% | — |
| Borrowings | 575 | 494 | 592 | 711 | 931 | 757 (Sep-26) |
| CFO | 17 | 284 | 199 | 153 | 277 | — |
| Debtor days | 93 | 66 | 85 | 55 | 98 | — |

| Quarter | Sep25 | Dec25 | Mar26 | Jun26 | Sep26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 1,262 | 1,371 | 1,667 | 1,310 | 1,384 |
| OPM | 10% | 10% | 10% | 11% | 10% |
| PAT | 37 | 53 | 78 | 57 | 58 |

No loss quarter. PAT grew YoY in every one of the last 8 quarters; Q2 FY27 PAT was +57% YoY.

**Shareholding (Sep-24 → Sep-26):**
- Promoter 66.48% → 61.48%. The fall is fully explained by the preferential allotment; no promoter selling.
- FII 4.39% → 10.31%.
- DII 0.24% → 2.41%.
- Institutions are rising. No promoter pledge was found (no-encumbrance declaration as of Mar-26).

**Structural story (named cause):** OPM is flat at 10%, so this is **not** a margin step-change. The step-change is in **ROCE (9–12% → 21–24%) and PAT (₹25 cr → ₹246 cr)**. It came from operating leverage on a tower/monopole plant whose utilisation jumped as PGCIL/ISTS EPC orders arrived. Specifically:
- Record order book of **₹10,066 cr (1.76x TTM revenue)** at Sep-26.
- Record Q2 inflow of ₹2,111 cr (+70% YoY), including ₹1,054 cr exports.
- A 75,000 MTPA capacity expansion is underway.
- The ₹433.5 cr equity raise paid down debt (₹327.5 cr earmarked; borrowings ₹931 → ₹757 cr).

**Bull case (numbers):** FY27–29 PAT CAGR of 25%, slightly below the company's ~30% FY27 guide, takes PAT to about ₹420 cr by FY29. At 20x that is about ₹8,400 cr mcap, roughly 1.4x from here in about 2.5 yrs. At 25x with 30% CAGR it is about 2x. Multibagger only if exports and the new EPC arm (Evergrid India, incorporated 4-Nov-26) lift OPM above 11%.

**Risks:**
- Margin ceiling of 10% (steel pass-through). EPC margins are thin.
- Debtor days 55 → 98 in FY26.
- History of single-digit ROCE (FY20–22). This is a cyclical business, not a franchise.
- Polymer-pipes segment is a distraction.

body:
`insight:india-2021-new-age-ipo-vintage` | confidence: verified | date: 2022-02-16 | tickers: PAYTM, NYKAA, POLICYBZR, ETERNAL, LICI

2021 was then India's best-ever year for IPO fundraising (Business Today year-ender). By 30 Dec 2021, 45 of 65 IPOs were above issue and 15 had doubled - the 'listing pop' peak. The marquee loss-making tech listings then de-rated in 2022: Paytm (issue Rs2,150, Nov-2021, largest IPO to that date) was at ~Rs864 (-60%) by Feb 2022 and later fell further; Nykaa (issue Rs1,125, listed ~Rs2,206, peaked ~Rs2,573) was ~21% below issue (bonus-adjusted) in 2023; PB Fintech (issue Rs980, +22.7% on day one) ~22% below issue by Feb 2022; Zomato (issue Rs76, peaked ~Rs169) fell >50% to ~Rs82 by Feb 2022 before turning into a large winner by 2024 as quick commerce scaled and it turned profitable. LIC (May-2022, issue Rs949) listed at Rs867 (-8.6%). Client Associates' later study found companies 'with clear profitability paths, revenue scaling, and margin improvements significantly outperformed', while cash-burning firms lost value. Lesson: in a hot vintage, the issue price embeds the peak multiple; the long-run outcome then splits on whether unit economics turn positive (Zomato, PB Fintech recovered; Paytm suffered a regulatory blow in Jan-2024 RBI action on Paytm Payments Bank). Early signal visible at the time: losses + high OFS share (PE/VC exits) + price set on revenue multiples. Prices quoted are snapshot values from dated articles, not current.

`insight:india-liquidity-fpi-vs-dii` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-11-19

Who sets the marginal price has changed. Calendar 2025: FPIs sold a record ~Rs1.5-2.0 lakh crore of Indian equities (NSDL-based reports differ by cutoff: Rs1.51 tn YTD mid-Dec per Business Standard; Rs2.03 tn full year per Angel One citing NSDL), while DIIs bought a record ~Rs6 lakh crore+ (highest since BSE data began in 2007; Rs5.26 tn in 2024). SIP inflows (AMFI, as reported) were ~Rs3.34 lakh crore in 2025 vs ~Rs2.68 lakh crore in 2024, with monthly SIP records around Rs26-32k crore through 2025-26. Oct-2024 was itself a then-record FPI monthly outflow (>$8.5bn by mid-month). 2026: after the Gulf conflict began in late Feb-2026, FPIs pulled ~$12.6bn in March alone (Finnovate/NSDL, single-source) and the Nifty fell ~15% Jan-Mar 2026; blogs report 2026 YTD FPI outflow already exceeding 2025 (unverified). Interpretation: (1) DII/SIP flows dampen drawdowns and keep domestic valuations above EM peers, but they are pro-cyclical too - SIP stoppage ratios rise after weak years; (2) FPI flows still drive large caps (banks, IT) and the rupee; (3) persistent domestic flows can keep 'expensive stays expensive' longer than value investors expect, which also lowers future returns. Actionable: track monthly NSDL FPI net flows, AMFI SIP gross flows and SIP stoppage ratio as a liquidity dashboard; a simultaneous FPI exodus and falling SIP flows is the setup for deeper Indian drawdowns.

Sources:

body: False alarms had a mechanism an outsider could check without relying on the company's own accounts: store counts, subscribers, gold inventory, a sovereign debtor, listed investee prices. In those cases the cash eventually arrived and governance was clean or improving. In the traps, the good number could only be checked through company-supplied data (cash, partner profits, distributors, group receivables). The cash never arrived, and governance flags such as auditor exits, promoter stake falls and related-party deals were present. Many false alarms were only *half* false. A high P/E was benign for the business but bit the price once it reached about 2x the stock's own median: DMart, Asian Paints, Pidilite, Page, Bajaj Finance and HDFC Bank each had 4-6 flat years after their peak multiples.
